verses.zh: 原来前约有礼拜的条例和属世界的圣幕。
verses.en: Now the first covenant,[NOTE:1] in fact, had regulations for worship and its earthly sanctuary.
notes: Grk “the first” (referring to the covenant described in Heb 8:7, 13). In the translation the referent (covenant) has been specified for clarity.

verses.zh: 因为有预备的帐幕，头一层叫作圣所，里面有灯台、桌子，和陈设饼。
verses.en: For a tent was prepared, the outer one,[NOTE:1] which contained[NOTE:2] the lampstand, the table, and the presentation of the loaves; this[NOTE:3] is called the Holy Place.
notes: Grk “the first,” in order of approach in the ritual.
Grk “in which [were].”
Grk “which,” describing the outer tent.

verses.zh: 第二幔子后又有一层帐幕，叫作至圣所，
verses.en: And after the second curtain there was a tent called the holy of holies.

verses.zh: 有金香炉（炉：或译坛），有包金的约柜，柜里有盛吗哪的金罐和亚伦发过芽的杖，并两块约版；
verses.en: It contained the golden altar of incense and the ark of the covenant covered entirely with gold. In this ark[NOTE:1] were the golden urn containing the manna, Aaron’s rod that budded, and the stone tablets of the covenant.
notes: Grk “in which”; in the translation the referent (the ark) has been specified for clarity.

verses.zh: 柜上面有荣耀基路伯的影罩着施恩（施恩：原文是蔽罪）座。这几件我现在不能一一细说。
verses.en: And above the ark[NOTE:1] were the cherubim[NOTE:2] of glory overshadowing the mercy seat. Now is not the time to speak of these things in detail.
notes: Grk “above it”; in the translation the referent (the ark) has been specified for clarity.

The cherubim (pl.) were an order of angels mentioned repeatedly in the OT but only here in the NT. They were associated with God’s presence, glory, and holiness. Their images that sat on top of the ark of the covenant are described in Exod 25:18-20.

verses.zh: 这些物件既如此预备齐了，众祭司就常进头一层帐幕，行拜　神的礼。
verses.en: So with these things prepared like this, the priests enter continually into the outer tent[NOTE:1] as they perform their duties.
notes: Grk “the first tent.”

verses.zh: 至于第二层帐幕，惟有大祭司一年一次独自进去，没有不带着血为自己和百姓的过错献上。
verses.en: But only the high priest enters once a year into the inner tent,[NOTE:1] and not without blood that he offers for himself and for the sins of the people committed in ignorance.[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “the second tent.”

Or perhaps “the unintentional sins of the people”; Grk “the ignorances of the people.” Cf. BDAG 13 s.v. ἀγνόημα, “sin committed in ignorance/unintentionally.” This term seems to be simply a synonym for “sins” (cf. Heb 5:2) and does not pick up the distinction made in Num 15:22-31 between unwitting sin and “high-handed” sin. The Day of Atonement ritual in Lev 16 covered all the sins of the people, not just the unwitting ones.

verses.zh: 圣灵用此指明，头一层帐幕仍存的时候，进入至圣所的路还未显明。
verses.en: The Holy Spirit is making clear that the way into the Holy Place had not yet appeared as long as the old tabernacle[NOTE:1] was standing.
notes: Grk “the first tent.” The literal phrase “the first tent” refers to either (1) the outer chamber of the tabernacle in the wilderness (as in vv. 2, 6) or (2) the entire tabernacle as a symbol of the OT system of approaching God. The second is more likely given the contrast that follows in vv. 11-12.

verses.zh: 那头一层帐幕作现今的一个表样，所献的礼物和祭物，就着良心说，都不能叫礼拜的人得以完全。
verses.en: This was a symbol for the time then present, when gifts and sacrifices were offered that could not perfect the conscience of the worshiper.

verses.zh: 这些事，连那饮食和诸般洗濯的规矩，都不过是属肉体的条例，命定到振兴的时候为止。
verses.en: They served only for matters of food and drink[NOTE:1] and various ritual washings; they are external regulations[NOTE:2] imposed until the new order came.[NOTE:3]
notes: Grk “only for foods and drinks.”

Most witnesses (D1 M) have “various washings, and external regulations” (βαπτισμοῖς καὶ δικαιώμασιν, baptismois kai dikaiōmasin), with both nouns in the dative. The translation “washings; they are…regulations” renders βαπτισμοῖς, δικαιώματα (baptismois, dikaiōmata; found in such significant mss as P46 א* A I P 0278 33 1739 1881 al sa) in which case δικαιώματα is taken as the nominative subject of the participle ἐπικείμενα (epikeimena). It seems far more likely that scribes would conform δικαιώματα to the immediately preceding datives and join it to them by καί than they would to the following nominative participle. Both on external and internal evidence the text is thus secure as reading βαπτισμοῖς, δικαιώματα.
Grk “until the time of setting things right.”

verses.zh: 但现在基督已经来到，作了将来美事的大祭司，经过那更大更全备的帐幕，不是人手所造，也不是属乎这世界的；
verses.en: But now Christ has come[NOTE:1] as the high priest of the good things to come. He passed through the greater and more perfect tent not made with hands, that is, not of this creation,
notes: Grk “But Christ, when he came,” introducing a sentence that includes all of Heb 9:11-12. The main construction is “Christ, having come…, entered…, having secured…,” and everything else describes his entrance.

verses.zh: 并且不用山羊和牛犊的血，乃用自己的血，只一次进入圣所，成了永远赎罪的事。
verses.en: and he entered once for all into the Most Holy Place not by the blood of goats and calves but by his own blood, and so he himself secured[NOTE:1] eternal redemption.
notes: This verb occurs in the Greek middle voice, which here intensifies the role of the subject, Christ, in accomplishing the action: “he alone secured”; “he and no other secured.”

verses.zh: 若山羊和公牛的血，并母牛犊的灰，洒在不洁的人身上，尚且叫人成圣，身体洁净，
verses.en: For if the blood of goats and bulls and the ashes of a young cow sprinkled on those who are defiled consecrated them and provided ritual purity,[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “for the purifying of the flesh.” The “flesh” here is symbolic of outward or ritual purity in contrast to inner purity, that of the conscience (cf. Heb 9:9).

verses.zh: 何况基督藉着永远的灵，将自己无瑕无疵献给　神，他的血岂不更能洗净你们的心（原文是良心），除去你们的死行，使你们事奉那永生　神吗？
verses.en: how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without blemish to God, purify our[NOTE:1] consciences from dead works to worship the living God.
notes: The reading adopted by the translation is attested by many authorities (A D* K P 365 1739* al). But many others (א D2 0278 33 1739c 1881 M lat sa) read “your” instead of “our.” The diversity of evidence makes this a difficult case to decide from external evidence alone. The first and second person pronouns differ by only one letter in Greek, as in English, also making this problem difficult to decide based on internal evidence and transcriptional probability. In the context, the author’s description of sacrificial activities seems to invite the reader to compare his own possible participation in OT liturgy as over against the completed work of Christ, so the second person pronoun “your” might make more sense. On the other hand, TCGNT 599 argues that “our” is preferable because the author of Hebrews uses direct address (i.e., the second person) only in the hortatory sections. What is more, the author seems to prefer the first person in explanatory remarks or when giving the logical grounds for an assertion (cf. Heb 4:15; 7:14). It is hard to reach a definitive conclusion in this case, but the data lean slightly in favor of the first person pronoun.

verses.zh: 为此，他作了新约的中保，既然受死赎了人在前约之时所犯的罪过，便叫蒙召之人得着所应许永远的产业。
verses.en: And so he is the mediator[NOTE:1] of a new covenant, so that those who are called may receive the eternal inheritance he has promised,[NOTE:2] since he died[NOTE:3] to set them free from the violations committed under the first covenant.
notes: The Greek word μεσίτης (mesitēs, “mediator”) in this context does not imply that Jesus was a mediator in the contemporary sense of the word, i.e., he worked for compromise between opposing parties. Here the term describes his function as the one who was used by God to enact a new covenant which established a new relationship between God and his people, but entirely on God’s terms.
Grk “the promise of the eternal inheritance.”
Grk “a death having occurred.”

verses.zh: 凡有遗命必须等到留遗命（遗命：原文与约字同）的人死了；
verses.en: For where there is a will, the death of the one who made it must be proven.[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “there is a necessity for the death of the one who made it to be proven.”

verses.zh: 因为人死了，遗命才有效力，若留遗命的尚在，那遗命还有用处吗？
verses.en: For a will takes effect only at death, since it carries no force while the one who made it is alive.

verses.zh: 所以，前约也不是不用血立的；
verses.en: So even the first covenant was inaugurated with blood.[NOTE:1]
notes: The Greek text reinforces this by negating the opposite (“not even the first covenant was inaugurated without blood”), but this double negation is not used in contemporary English.

verses.zh: 因为摩西当日照着律法将各样诫命传给众百姓，就拿朱红色绒和牛膝草，把牛犊山羊的血和水洒在书上，又洒在众百姓身上，说：
verses.en: For when Moses had spoken every command to all the people according to the law, he took the blood of calves and goats with water and scarlet wool and hyssop and sprinkled both the book itself and all the people,

verses.zh: 「这血就是　神与你们立约的凭据。」
verses.en: and said, “This is the blood of the covenant that God has commanded you to keep.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “which God commanded for you (or in your case).”sn A quotation from Exod 24:8.

verses.zh: 他又照样把血洒在帐幕和各样器皿上。
verses.en: And both the tabernacle and all the utensils of worship he likewise sprinkled with blood.

verses.zh: 按着律法，凡物差不多都是用血洁净的；若不流血，罪就不得赦免了。
verses.en: Indeed according to the law almost everything was purified with blood, and without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness.

verses.zh: 照着天上样式做的物件必须用这些祭物去洁净；但那天上的本物自然当用更美的祭物去洁净。
verses.en: So it was necessary for the sketches[NOTE:1] of the things in heaven to be purified with these sacrifices,[NOTE:2] but the heavenly things themselves required[NOTE:3] better sacrifices than these.
notes: Or “prototypes,” “outlines,” referring to the earthly sanctuary. See Heb 8:5 above for the prior use of this term.
Grk “with these”; in the translation the referent (sacrifices) has been specified for clarity.
Grk “the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these.”

verses.zh: 因为基督并不是进了人手所造的圣所（这不过是真圣所的影像），乃是进了天堂，如今为我们显在　神面前；
verses.en: For Christ did not enter a sanctuary made with hands—the representation[NOTE:1] of the true sanctuary[NOTE:2]—but into heaven itself, and he appears now in God’s presence for us.
notes: Or “prefiguration.”
The word “sanctuary” is not in the Greek text at this point, but has been supplied for clarity.

verses.zh: 也不是多次将自己献上，像那大祭司每年带着牛羊的血（牛羊的血：原文作不是自己的血）进入圣所，
verses.en: And he did not enter to offer[NOTE:1] himself again and again, the way the high priest enters the sanctuary year after year with blood that is not his own,
notes: Grk “and not that he might offer,” continuing the previous construction.

verses.zh: 如果这样，他从创世以来，就必多次受苦了。但如今在这末世显现一次，把自己献为祭，好除掉罪。
verses.en: for then he would have had to suffer again and again since the foundation of the world. But now he has appeared once for all at the consummation of the ages to put away sin by his sacrifice.

verses.zh: 按着定命，人人都有一死，死后且有审判。
verses.en: And just as people[NOTE:1] are appointed to die once, and then to face judgment,[NOTE:2]
notes: Here ἀνθρώποις (anthrōpois) has been translated as a generic noun (“people”).
Grk “and after this—judgment.”

verses.zh: 像这样，基督既然一次被献，担当了多人的罪，将来要向那等候他的人第二次显现，并与罪无关，乃是为拯救他们。
verses.en: so also, after Christ was offered once to bear the sins of many,[NOTE:1] to those who eagerly await him he will appear a second time, not to bear sin[NOTE:2] but to bring salvation.[NOTE:3]
notes: An allusion to Isa 53:12.
Grk “without sin,” but in context this does not refer to Christ’s sinlessness (as in Heb 4:15) but to the fact that sin is already dealt with by his first coming.
Grk “for salvation.” This may be construed with the verb “await” (those who wait for him to bring them salvation), but the connection with “appear” (as in the translation) is more likely.
